paragraphs: Scouting Ireland is a big group for young people. It has about 40,000 members in 400 local groups. Now it has a big money problem.
Many years ago, some children were harmed by adults in older scout groups. More than 350 people have now spoken about this. Over 70 of them went to court to ask for money.
Each case can cost about €250,000. So the group needs about €8 million.
It may sell some empty buildings. It may also get a big loan from a bank. It may ask each local group for €10,000 to €20,000. Volunteers say this means a lot of hard work.
The Government says the State will not pay. The group has enough money until the end of next year. Its leader says it is still working well. Nothing is decided yet.
sentZh: 愛爾蘭童軍是一個大型的青少年團體。
它在400個地方團體中約有4萬名成員。
現在它遇到了很大的財務問題。
多年前，一些孩子在較早的童軍團體中受到成年人的傷害。
現在已有超過350人說出了這件事。
其中70多人上法院要求賠償。
每個案件可能花費約25萬歐元。
所以這個團體需要大約800萬歐元。
它可能會賣掉一些空置的建築物。
它也可能向銀行借一大筆貸款。
它可能會要求每個地方團體拿出1萬到2萬歐元。
志工說這代表要付出很多辛勞。
政府表示國家不會支付。
這個團體的錢足夠用到明年年底。
它的領導人說組織仍運作良好。
目前還沒有做出任何決定。

paragraphs: Scouting Ireland, the country's biggest youth group, is looking at emergency plans to raise €8 million. The money would pay survivors of child abuse that happened many years ago. It would also help the organisation to survive. The plans are in private documents seen by The Irish Times.

A report from 7 November warned that the size and timing of legal claims are a serious money risk. If the group cannot pay its bills on time, the board may have to close it down, unless there is a good plan to change how it is run.

The plan has three parts. Scouting Ireland could sell empty buildings and take out a large bank loan. It would also ask its local groups to lend between €10,000 and €20,000 each to the national office. Volunteers say this would mean a lot of fundraising.

More than 350 people say they were abused as children in two older scout groups. These groups joined together in 2004 to form Scouting Ireland. Over 70 survivors have gone to court, and several cases ended this year with payments. One case can cost close to €250,000, including legal fees.
The document says the group has no other way to find money. The Government has said clearly that the State is not responsible for the past abuse.

The latest accounts show that Scouting Ireland has enough money until the end of next year. Its chair, Aidan Magner, says the group can still pay its way and wants to grow. Nothing has been decided yet.
sentZh: 愛爾蘭童軍是全國最大的青少年團體，正在研究籌集800萬歐元的緊急計畫。
這筆錢將用來賠償多年前兒童受虐事件的倖存者。
它也將幫助這個組織存續下去。
這些計畫寫在《愛爾蘭時報》看到的內部文件中。
一份11月7日的報告警告，法律索賠的規模和時機是嚴重的財務風險。
報告說，如果這個團體無法按時支付帳單，理事會可能必須將它關閉，除非有一個改變其運作方式的好計畫。
這項計畫分成三部分。
愛爾蘭童軍可能出售空置的建築，並向銀行申請大筆貸款。
它也會要求各地方團體各借給全國辦公室1萬至2萬歐元。
志工表示，這將需要大量募款。
超過350人表示，他們小時候在兩個較早的童軍團體中受到虐待。
這兩個團體在2004年合併，組成了愛爾蘭童軍。
已有70多名倖存者提告，今年有數個案件以賠償了結。
一個案件連同律師費可能花費近25萬歐元。
文件指出，這個團體已沒有其他籌錢的方法。
政府已清楚表示，國家不需要為過去的虐待事件負責。
最新的財務報表顯示，愛爾蘭童軍的資金足以維持到明年年底。
理事會主席艾登·麥格納表示，這個團體仍能自給自足，並希望繼續成長。
目前尚未做出任何決定。

paragraphs: Scouting Ireland is considering emergency measures to raise €8 million so that it can compensate survivors of historical child abuse and avoid a possible collapse, according to confidential internal documents seen by The Irish Times.

An internal briefing dated 7 November warned that the timing and scale of legal claims posed a significant financial risk. It stated that if the organisation could not meet its liabilities when they fell due, the board would be obliged to begin liquidation unless a credible restructuring plan was in place.

Under the proposals, the youth organisation would sell vacant properties and secure a sizeable bank loan. Local scout groups would also be asked to voluntarily advance between €10,000 and €20,000 each to the national office. Volunteers said this would require major fundraising at local level.
The document says other sources of funding have been exhausted. It also notes that the Government has firmly rejected any suggestion that the State is liable for the past abuse.

More than 350 people have come forward to say they were abused as children in the Catholic Boy Scouts of Ireland and the Scout Association of Ireland, which merged in 2004. More than 70 survivors have taken civil cases, and several long-running cases were settled this year as trial dates approached. The average settlement, including legal fees, can be close to €250,000.

The latest accounts show enough money to operate until the end of next year. Board chair Aidan Magner said the organisation was operationally solvent and focused on expansion, describing a programme to rebuild its cash reserves. Scouting Ireland has about 40,000 members in 400 local groups. No final decision on the measures has been reported.
sentZh: 根據《愛爾蘭時報》看到的機密內部文件，愛爾蘭童軍正考慮採取緊急措施籌集800萬歐元，以賠償過去兒童受虐事件的倖存者，並避免可能的倒閉。
一份日期為11月7日的內部簡報警告，法律索賠的時機與規模構成重大財務風險。
簡報指出，若該組織無法在債務到期時償還，除非有可信的重組計畫，否則理事會將有義務啟動清算。
根據這些提案，這個青少年組織將出售空置房產並取得一筆可觀的銀行貸款。
各地方童軍團體也將被要求自願向全國辦公室預付1萬至2萬歐元。
志工表示，這將需要在地方層面進行大規模募款。
文件說其他資金來源已經用盡。
文件也指出，政府已堅決拒絕任何關於國家須為過去虐待事件負責的說法。
超過350人站出來表示，他們小時候在愛爾蘭天主教男童軍和愛爾蘭童軍協會中受到虐待，這兩個組織於2004年合併。
已有70多名倖存者提起民事訴訟，今年有數宗長期案件在開庭日期臨近時達成和解。
包括律師費在內，平均和解金額可能接近25萬歐元。
最新的財務報表顯示，資金足以運作到明年年底。
理事會主席艾登·麥格納表示，該組織在運作上仍具償債能力，並專注於擴張，他還介紹了一項重建現金儲備的計畫。
愛爾蘭童軍在400個地方團體中約有4萬名成員。
目前尚無關於這些措施的最終決定的報導。

paragraphs: Scouting Ireland is weighing a raft of emergency measures to raise €8 million, both to compensate survivors of historical child abuse and to stave off a possible collapse, according to confidential internal papers obtained by The Irish Times.

A briefing dated 7 November cautioned that the timing and magnitude of legal claims represented a considerable financial threat. Should the organisation prove unable to meet its liabilities as they fall due, it said, the board would be duty-bound to initiate liquidation in the absence of a credible restructuring.

The proposed rescue package hinges on offloading vacant properties and securing a substantial bank loan. In addition, local scout groups would be invited to advance between €10,000 and €20,000 apiece to the national office, a request that volunteers say would entail an intensive fundraising drive.
According to the document, alternative funding avenues have been exhausted, and the Government has flatly rejected any notion that the State bears vicarious liability for past abuse.

Upwards of 350 people have come forward alleging abuse as children in the two legacy bodies, which amalgamated in 2004 to form Scouting Ireland. Over 70 survivors have pursued civil actions, and several protracted cases were settled this year on the eve of trial, with average settlements, legal costs included, approaching €250,000.

The most recent accounts indicate sufficient funds to keep operating until the end of next year. Board chair Aidan Magner insisted the organisation remained operationally solvent and was intent on expansion, pointing to a financial resilience programme designed to replenish cash reserves. The measures, which would affect some 40,000 members across 400 groups, remain at the proposal stage.
sentZh: 根據《愛爾蘭時報》取得的機密內部文件，愛爾蘭童軍正在權衡一連串緊急措施以籌集800萬歐元，既用於賠償過去兒童受虐事件的倖存者，也為了避免可能的倒閉。
一份日期為11月7日的簡報警告，法律索賠的時機與規模構成相當大的財務威脅。
簡報表示，若該組織無法在債務到期時償還，在缺乏可信重組方案的情況下，理事會將有責任啟動清算。
擬議的救援方案取決於出售空置房產和取得一筆大額銀行貸款。
此外，各地方童軍團體將被邀請各自向全國辦公室預付1萬至2萬歐元，志工表示這項請求將需要密集的募款活動。
據文件所述，其他資金管道已經用盡，而政府已斷然否定國家須為過去虐待事件承擔轉承責任的說法。
超過350人站出來指稱自己小時候在兩個前身組織中受到虐待，這兩個組織於2004年合併成為愛爾蘭童軍。
70多名倖存者已提起民事訴訟，今年有數宗曠日持久的案件在開庭前夕和解，平均和解金額連同律師費接近25萬歐元。
最近的財務報表顯示，資金足以維持運作到明年年底。
理事會主席艾登·麥格納堅稱，該組織在運作上仍有償債能力，並決心擴張，他指出有一項旨在補充現金儲備的財務韌性計畫。
這些措施將影響400個團體中約4萬名成員，目前仍處於提案階段。

paragraphs: Scouting Ireland is reportedly contemplating a series of emergency measures intended to generate €8 million, with the dual objective of compensating survivors of historical child abuse and averting the potential collapse of the organisation. These proposals are outlined in confidential internal documentation examined by The Irish Times.

A briefing dated 7 November emphasised that the timing and magnitude of outstanding legal claims constituted a substantial financial risk. Consequently, should the organisation be unable to discharge its liabilities as they fall due, the board would be legally obliged to commence liquidation, unless a credible restructuring could be implemented.

The proposed strategy is contingent upon three principal elements: the disposal of vacant properties, the acquisition of a considerable bank loan and voluntary contributions of between €10,000 and €20,000 from each local group. Volunteers have nevertheless indicated that such contributions would necessitate extensive fundraising.

The document asserts that alternative sources of finance have been exhausted. Furthermore, the Government has unequivocally rejected the proposition that the State bears vicarious liability for historical abuse.

In total, more than 350 individuals have disclosed that they were abused as children within the two predecessor organisations, which merged in 2004. Over 70 survivors have initiated civil proceedings, and a number of protracted cases were resolved this year shortly before trial. The average settlement, inclusive of legal fees, may approach €250,000.

Although the most recent accounts indicate adequate funds until the end of next year, additional resources would subsequently be required. Board chair Aidan Magner maintained that the organisation is operationally solvent and committed to expansion, citing a financial resilience programme. Approximately 40,000 members across 400 groups could ultimately be affected, although no definitive decision has been made.

這些提案載於《愛爾蘭時報》檢視的機密內部文件中。
一份日期為11月7日的簡報強調，尚未解決的法律索賠在時機與規模上構成重大財務風險。

擬議策略取決於三大要素：出售空置房產、取得一筆可觀的銀行貸款，以及每個地方團體自願出資1萬至2萬歐元。
然而志工指出，這樣的出資將需要大規模的募款。
文件聲稱其他資金來源已經用盡。
此外，政府已明確否定國家須為過去虐待事件承擔轉承責任的主張。
總計已有超過350人透露，他們小時候在兩個於2004年合併的前身組織中受到虐待。
70多名倖存者已提起民事訴訟，今年有若干拖延已久的案件在開庭前不久獲得解決。
包括律師費在內，平均和解金額可能接近25萬歐元。
雖然最近的財務報表顯示資金足以維持到明年年底，但之後將需要額外的資源。
理事會主席艾登·麥格納堅稱，該組織在運作上具償債能力並致力於擴張，並舉出一項財務韌性計畫為證。
400個團體中約4萬名成員最終可能受到影響，不過目前尚未做出明確決定。
